questions.question: Compare preservation by osmosis with high or low temperature, highlighting advantages, limitations, and suitable foods for each method. / [CO4]
questions.solution_html: • Compare preservation by osmosis with high or low temperature, highlighting advantages, limitations, and suitable foods for each method. [A]/ [CO4] (2 marks each for each aspects) Aspect Osmosis (salting/sugaring) High Temperature Low Temperature Definition Preservation by using salt or sugar to draw out water from food and microbes Preservation by applying heat to destroy microorganisms and enzymes Preservation by using low temperatures to slow microbial and enzyme activity Principle Removes water from food and microbes by osmotic pressure Destroys microorganisms and inactivates enzymes Slows microbial growth and enzyme activity Advantages Simple, inexpensive, improves taste, no refrigeration needed Ensures safety, increases shelf life Preserves freshness and nutrients Limitations Alters taste/texture; not suitable for all foods Loss of some nutrients; may affect flavour Needs electricity; limited shelf life in refrigeration Suitable Foods Pickles, jams, jellies, salted fish Milk, canned foods, cooked foods Fruits, vegetables, meat, leftovers

questions.question: Classify milk and milk products. Explain their nutritive composition and importance in growth and development. / [CO3] [10x1 = 10]
questions.solution_html:
• Classify milk and milk products. Explain their nutritive composition and importance in
  • growth and development. [K] / [CO3]
  • Classification of Milk and Milk Products (4 marks)
  • A. Based on Fat Content / Standardization
  • • Whole milk: ~3.5–6% fat
  • • Toned milk: ~3% fat
  • • Double-toned milk: ~1.5% fat
  • • Skimmed milk: <0.5% fat
  • • Full-cream milk: ~6% fat
  • B. Based on Processing
  • • Pasteurized milk: Heated to destroy pathogens
  • • Sterilized milk: Longer shelf life, slight nutrient loss
  • • UHT milk: Long shelf life, minimal nutrient loss
  • • Homogenized milk: Uniform texture, no cream separation
  • • Reconstituted milk: Made from milk powder
  • • Concentrated products: Condensed milk, evaporated milk
  • C. Fermented Milk Products
  • • Curd, yoghurt, buttermilk, kefir
  • Nutritive Composition of Milk (per 100 ml) (4 marks)
  • • Energy: 60–70 kcal
  • • Protein: ~3.2 g (high biological value)
  • • Fat: 3.5–4 g
  • • Carbohydrates: ~4.8 g (lactose)
  • • Minerals: Calcium (120 mg), phosphorus, potassium
  • • Vitamins: A, D, B2, B12
  • • Water: 85–88%
  • Importance in Growth and Development (2 marks)
  • • Promotes bone and teeth formation (rich in calcium & phosphorus)
  • • Supports growth and tissue repair (high-quality protein)
  • • Important for children, adolescents, and pregnant women
  • • Helps in overall body development and maintenance
  • [10x1 = 10]
